title: Choosing a University Major
paragraphs: Torn between studying engineering, which his family expected, and studying literature, which genuinely interested him, Faris spent his entire final year of high school feeling paralyzed by the decision.
He eventually spoke honestly with his father, who admitted he had actually wanted to study history himself decades earlier but had felt pressured into engineering by his own parents at the time.

This conversation surprised Faris and gave him the confidence to choose literature, despite some initial disappointment from extended family members who had assumed he would follow a more traditional path.
Years later, working as a published writer, Faris often reflects that an honest conversation with his father changed the direction of his entire life more than any single exam or class ever could.
